definitions.ISSUE-01: Classification of murder as first degree without planning and deliberation via the s 231(5) constructive route (death caused while committing s 279 forcible confinement).
definitions.ISSUE-02: Mandatory life sentence on a murder conviction and the appellate treatment of a trial judge's constitutional exemption from the mandatory minimum.
definitions.ISSUE-03: Reverse-onus statutory presumptions and the presumption of innocence: what burden and standard of proof falls on the accused.
definitions.PROP-01: Irrespective of planning and deliberation, murder is first degree when the death is caused while the accused is committing or attempting an enumerated offence, including s 279 kidnapping and forcible confinement.
definitions.PROP-02: Murder carries a mandatory sentence of life imprisonment; the trial judge's constitutional exemption from the mandatory minimum was reversed on appeal and the mandatory minimum imposed.
definitions.PROP-03: A reverse-onus presumption places a legal (persuasive) burden on the accused to disprove the presumed fact on a balance of probabilities, engaging the constitutionally entrenched presumption of innocence in s 11(d).
definitions.CONCLUSION-01: The Crown's forcible-confinement theory can support first degree murder even absent planning and deliberation.
definitions.CONCLUSION-02: The supplied appellate authorities sustained a constitutional exemption from the mandatory minimum sentence.
definitions.CLAIM-01: Planning and deliberation is always required before murder can be classified as first degree.
definitions.CLAIM-02: An accused rebutting a reverse-onus presumption must disprove the presumed fact beyond a reasonable doubt.
